svg.aria-label: Sources of capital for a Co-operative Society: Member Share Capital, Retained Statutory Reserves, Member Deposits, Entrance Fees, and External Loans or Grants
svg.text: How a Co-operative Society Raises Capital (Internal vs. External Sources)
Unlike Public LLCs, Co-operative shares do NOT trade on a Stock Exchange — they are bought/withdrawn directly through the Society at par value!
Internal Capital (Members' Equity)
1. Member Share Capital (Fixed Par Value)
Members buy affordable shares (e.g. $5–$10 par) often via
payroll deductions; legal cap limits any single member's share!
2. Statutory Reserve & Retained Surplus
Law requires transferring a % of yearly Net Surplus (often
20%–25%) into a Statutory Reserve + Education Fund!
Indivisible permanent safety cushion owned collectively!
3. Entrance / Registration Fees & Special Levies
Small one-time joining fee paid by new members (helps
cover setup admin or transfers to Statutory Reserve!)
External & Borrowed Capital (Liabilities)
1. Member Savings & Fixed Deposits
Members deposit extra savings (earning interest) which
Credit Unions lend onward to other members as loans!
2. Loans From Co-op League / Commercial Banks
Long-term mortgages or development loans from National
Co-op Leagues, Credit Union Leagues, or Agricultural Banks
3. Government / Donor Grants & Subsidies
State/NGO grants supporting farming co-ops, cold storage,
or rural community development (often non-repayable!)
Journal Entries When Member Buys vs. Withdraws Co-op Shares:
Buy Shares: Dr Bank / Cr Members' Share Capital | Withdraw Shares: Dr Members' Share Capital / Cr Bank (Par Value!)
